summary: T-0612 [bug, столпы 1/3 — движок/бесшовность; defect is in a BPMN CASE MODEL (purchaseApproval / 'Закупки'), not the platform, per D-064]: a boundary timer (PT2M) guarding userTask task-fin ('Согласование финдиректора') was authored NON-INTERRUPTING (cancelActivity='false' — deliberate; BPMN's own default when absent is interrupting=true) with its escalation branch (task-esc, 'Эскалация: финдир молчит') dead-ending at its own endEvent instead of reconnecting to the main flow. Observed live 2026-07-01/07-02 (session memory: 'boundary-таймер PT2M реально сработал (non-interrupting эскалация)'): when the finance director approved BEFORE the deadline fired, the main token reached endEvent 'Заказ размещён', but the still-armed, never-cancelled boundary timer left the instance permanently unable to complete — act_hi_procinst.end_time stayed NULL forever, even though the product-visible outcome had already appeared (a zombie instance). REPO INVESTIGATION CONFIRMS исход (б): purchaseApproval is NOT committed anywhere in the repo (no seed/fixture/template — only descriptive code comments citing it as a live-observed example). It was hand-authored raw XML, POSTed directly to /api/process-defs -> /publish during live acceptance ('НЕ мышью по канвасу'), so it lives ONLY as tenant/Flowable state on the dev stand. The canvas modeler never sets cancelActivity and exposes no interrupting/non-interrupting UI control at all (bpmn-js's own default is interrupting=true), confirming the non-interrupting choice could only come from hand-authored XML. FIX: (1) a corrected BPMN artifact (docs/design/T-0612-purchaseApproval-fixed.bpmn20.xml.txt) reproducing the finance-approval+escalation slice with a converging exclusiveGateway (gw-fin-converge) that BOTH task-fin's normal completion and task-esc's completion flow into before the shared endEvent — chosen over flipping cancelActivity=true or a terminateEndEvent because the business semantics require the escalation to stay a non-critical REMINDER, never a takeover of the finance director's approval authority (ADR §2 D1/D2 full reasoning). (2) A genuine platform hardening: src/core/bpmn-linter.ts gains an additive check, checkTimerEscalationConvergence (new LintViolationType 'timer_escalation_no_convergence'), closing the narrow, high-value slice of a gap T-0456's own doc-comment already named ('a full reachability/path analysis is out of v1 scope') — scoped ONLY to non-interrupting boundary timers (the shape that produced this live defect), flagging an escalation branch that reaches its own endEvent without first reconverging with the guarded task's own downstream path. (3) A standalone Flowable smoke-test script proving the fix live (deploy -> start -> complete task-fin before the timer fires -> assert instance ENDED) — NOT run in this session (see FRICTION: shared dev Postgres/Flowable port occupied by a sibling worktree).

findings: FINDINGS: no twin defect found. The only other BPMN model in the repository, seed/vendor-crm/processes/customer-onboarding.bpmn, is strictly linear (start -> 4 tasks -> end, single sequenceFlow chain) with zero boundary events, zero timers, zero gateways — no candidate for the same non-interrupting-timer-without-convergence pattern. src/__tests__/fixtures/bpmn/* are adversarial XML-parser test fixtures (raw-object-binding corpus), unrelated to this defect class. config/flowable/processes/{choros-smoke,tel-linear}.bpmn20.xml were also checked — tel-linear.bpmn20.xml has an exclusiveGateway (DMN-driven approval threshold) but NO boundary timer at all; choros-smoke.bpmn20.xml is a minimal external-task smoke fixture, no timer/gateway. Conclusion: purchaseApproval's non-interrupting-timer-without-convergence pattern is unique to that one case; the new linter check (checkTimerEscalationConvergence) now guards against any FUTURE recurrence of this exact shape in any process authored or imported going forward, whether via canvas or hand-authored XML.

level1.p1_finding: formatJsonReadable() (web/src/lib/format.js:279-291), the generic renderer StatusBanner uses for non-string violations, does JSON.stringify(violation).slice(0,120)+'…'. It has no knowledge of LintViolation's dedicated human-readable .message field. Measured: the JSON prefix before the "message" key alone is 108 chars against a 120-char cap — at most ~12 chars of the carefully-authored fix-hint text can ever survive, for ANY lint violation type, not just this one. This is a systemic UI bug in the shared violation-banner rendering path (affects every publish-time lint failure across the whole product), not specific to T-0612's new check. Recommend: format.js gets a LintViolation-aware formatter that surfaces .message directly instead of falling through to generic JSON truncation.
level1.modeler_ui_cannot_author_defect_shape: Confirmed via source read (web/src/canvas/timer-deadline-panel.jsx, web/src/canvas/bpmn-palette-provider.js — zero hits for cancelActivity/interrupting in either) AND live canvas interaction: the modeler exposes deadline-kind/deadline/escalateTo controls but NO interrupting/non-interrupting (cancelActivity) control anywhere. A non-interrupting boundary timer can only be authored via hand-written/imported XML — matches the spec's own provenance finding. This is why Level 1 proof used the modeler's real 'Загрузить' file-import path (a genuine product mechanism, not a bypass) rather than mouse-driven canvas authoring.

scenario_b_supplementary_finding.description: Second instance (29bb45ad-7858-11f1-abdf-aaa9cc4b0546) was left running past the PT2M deadline so BOTH task-fin and the timer-fired task-esc were simultaneously open in the pool. Completed task-fin FIRST (while task-esc was still open, uncompleted) via the real inbox UI. Result: gw-fin-converge AND sf-converge-end DID fire (confirmed in historic-activity-instances), but the process INSTANCE did not end (historic endTime stayed null, runtime GET returned 200 not 404) until task-esc was ALSO completed afterward (second UI pass) — endTime then became 2026-07-05T10:04:53.865Z, endActivityId end-order-placed, runtime 404.
scenario_b_supplementary_finding.interpretation: NOT a regression of the T-0612 zombie bug (end_time_ eventually became non-null in both orderings — the original bug was end_time_ staying NULL FOREVER, which did not happen here). It IS a refinement of ADR-T0612 section 2 D2's own narrative, which only walks through 'task-esc completes -> instance ends, task-fin remains a stale but harmless OPEN TASK' and explicitly calls the reverse ordering an out-of-scope product-policy question. Live proof shows the reverse ordering (task-fin completes first, post-timer-fire) leaves the process INSTANCE itself (not just a task) non-terminal until task-esc is also resolved, because Flowable's boundary-timer-spawned task-esc execution is a separate concurrent execution under the same process-instance scope that must independently resolve before the instance-root is marked ended, regardless of the exclusiveGateway having already routed the other token to the end event. Recommend as a P2 follow-up: amend ADR-T0612 D2 to state explicitly that when BOTH branches are open simultaneously, the instance requires both tasks resolved (in either order) to reach a terminal state, not just 'whichever finishes last'.
